scope: Installed ViennaPS 4.6.2 public Python surface (audited) and the ViennaPS 4.7.0 release (evaluated, version-qualified) vs. ViennaPS Workbench schema 7 project API.

environment.probeMethod: python -c introspection of viennaps/viennaps.d2/viennaps.d3; each behavioural probe ran as its own subprocess with a 40-120 s wall clock timeout in /tmp/opencode (no workbench state touched)
environment.runtimePolicy: 4.6.2 is the production runtime; 4.7.0 is supported through the same backend with version-gated ALD surface diffusion and advancedOxidation controls.

classifications.exposed: Reachable from a submitted project today, with its user-facing parameters.
classifications.engine-model-not-exposed: A native process model with no workbench step, catalog entry or API field.
classifications.advanced-parameter-or-output-not-exposed: Reachable only partially, or output-only: parameters/outputs that exist in the engine but cannot be set or requested from JSON.
classifications.internal-or-not-user-facing: Native plumbing, base classes, callbacks or writer utilities. Not a user-facing modelling capability.
classifications.absent-in-engine: Not present in ViennaPS at all; only available in the SPX (Sentaurus Process Explorer) reference flows.

classes.constructor: IsotropicProcess(rate=1.0, maskMaterial=Material('Undefined')) | IsotropicProcess(rate=1.0, maskMaterials=[...]) | IsotropicProcess(materialRates={Material: float}, defaultRate=0.0)

classes.notes: No ray flux engine: worker pins FluxEngineType.CPU_DISK and never selects GPU for it.

classes.notes: Verified on CPU_DISK and GPU_DISK in 2D and 3D; seeds and raysPerPoint are solver fields.

classes.constructor: DirectionalProcess(direction, materialRates={Material:(directional,isotropic)}, ...) | (direction, directionalVelocity, isotropicVelocity=0, maskMaterial=Material('Mask'), calculateVisibility=True) | (direction, directionalVelocity, isotropicVelocity, maskMaterials, calculateVisibility) | (rateSets: Sequence[RateSet]) | (rateSet: RateSet)
classes.docSummary: Flux arriving along one primary direction plus an optional isotropic component.
classes.notes: The scalar overload remains the default for schema-5 `directional` steps. Providing the additive `rateSets` list builds real `viennaps.RateSet` objects and calls the native `DirectionalProcess(rateSets: Sequence[RateSet])` overload; the probe in worker/probe_ratesets_native.py verifies additive directional and isotropic velocities, per-set maskMaterials and per-set calculateVisibility in 2D and 3D. The per-material `materialRates` mapping overload stays unexposed.

exposed: rateSets[] -> RateSet(direction, directionalVelocity, isotropicVelocity, maskMaterials, calculateVisibility)

classes.notes: The worker itself supplies a fixed, audited linear-combination callback; submitted JSON only provides coefficients (defaultBySpecies / byMaterial). Callback invocation counts and mean fluxes are recorded per step.

exposed: addIonParticle (sourcePower, thetaR*, minAngle, B_sp, mean/sigma/threshold energy, inflectAngle, n)

classes.docSummary: Thermal silicon oxidation with a diffusion-reaction oxide solver and optional mask mechanics.
classes.notes: Duration is derived from timeHours; the step-level duration field is rejected for this model. B5 adds the optional steps[].advancedOxidation object with the four solver setters proven to change the native surface (cflFactor, mechanicsTolerance, couplingTolerance, simplePressureRelaxation) plus Si110. Omitted block => historical request hashes unchanged. Excluded with probe evidence: GPU mode, maxGridPoints, solve bounds, iteration caps, pressure/stokes tolerance, simpleVelocityRelaxation, mask mechanics and the model-level save helpers. See docs/oxidation-advanced-contract.md.

notExposed: setCouplingIterations (explicit default inert; lowered value fails to converge)
setMechanicsIterations (explicit default inert; lowered value fails to converge)
setPressureIterations / setStokesIterations (explicit defaults inert; lowered pressure fails)
setPressureTolerance / setStokesTolerance (needs a coupled mechanicsTolerance adjustment)
setSimpleVelocityRelaxation (no surface change above 1e-8 um in the controlled probes)
setMaxGridPoints (solver cap; below the solve region it raises, above it is inert)
setSolveBounds / clearSolveBounds (raw Cartesian indices; controlled probe hit empty solve region)
setMaskParameters / setMask* mechanics (no verified LOCOS surface on this host)
setGpuMode / setGpuPreconditioner (CPU-only batch; GPU oxidation unverified)
model-level saveSurfaceMesh / saveVolumeMesh helpers (the workbench writes through Domain)

classes.constructor: GeometricTrenchDeposition(trenchWidth, trenchDepth, depositionRate, bottomMed, a, b, n)
classes.docSummary: Analytic geometric trench-fill model (closed-form profile, no level-set flux).
classes.notes: Probe 2026-10-30: 2D completes; the identical call on a 3D domain aborts with SIGSEGV after 'Applying geometric model'. 2D only.

classes.constructor: CSVFileProcess(ratesFile: str, direction, offset, isotropicComponent=0.0, directionalComponent=1.0, maskMaterials=[Material('Mask')], calculateVisibility=True)
classes.docSummary: Directional+isotropic process whose rate is interpolated from a CSV rate grid.
classes.notes: Probe 2026-10-30: runs in 2D and 3D but prints 'Interpolation mode not set.' twice and proceeds, i.e. an unset interpolation mode is not an error. Needs a CSV upload asset plus an explicit interpolation enum; setCustomInterpolator is a Python callback and must stay out of the JSON API.

classes.docSummary: Rectangular particle-shape distribution applied as a geometric model.
exposedBy: step model:particleShape, shape:box (schema 7; no-mask deposit, geometry-mask etch)
classes.notes: Probe 2026-10-30 (A4 mask re-run): the no-mask overload moves the exposed surface by the L-infinity half-axis and ignores the process duration in 2D and 3D. addMaskMaterial is safe for negative (etch) displacement in 2D/3D: the mask is built from the project material level sets exactly like the native FinFET example, and the protected material does not move. Every non-empty mask with positive (deposition) displacement SIGSEGVs (returnCode -11) regardless of mask construction (material mask, raw viennals mask, applyToSingleMaterial, insertMask) and regardless of overlap (near, far, full-domain); ViennaLS 5.8.5 and 5.10.0 both keep the upstream TODO 'There are still issues with positive box distributions if there is a mask used!'. So the workbench passes addMaskMaterial only for etches and records the omitted mask materials for depositions.

classes.docSummary: Spherical particle-shape distribution applied as a geometric model.
exposedBy: step model:particleShape, shape:sphere (schema 7; no-mask deposit, geometry-mask etch)
classes.notes: Probe 2026-10-30 (A4 mask re-run): the no-mask overload moves the exposed surface by the radius and ignores the process duration in 2D and 3D. addMaskMaterial is safe for negative (etch) displacement in 2D/3D (the native FinFET pattern); masked deposition SIGSEGVs (returnCode -11) for material masks, raw viennals masks, applyToSingleMaterial and insertMask, whether the mask is near, far or covers the whole domain. ViennaPS 4.7.0 / ViennaLS 5.10.0 still crash identically. So radius plus etch-only addMaskMaterial are exposed; the raw mask argument is not.

classes.docSummary: Multi-radius sphere distribution.
classes.notes: Probe 2026-10-30 (re-run for A4): aborts in 2D and 3D with returnCode -6, 'terminate called after throwing an instance of std::runtime_error' / 'what(): Point ID 3 is out of bounds for CustomSphereDistribution with 3 radii!', with and without a mask. It indexes one radius per surface point, so no bounded project-derived parameterization exists; stays unexposed.

classes.docSummary: Generic composable process model: users assemble surface, geometric and velocity models themselves.
classes.notes: Extension hook. Exposing it would let a project recombine native sub-models in ways no evidence covers; the workbench only instantiates concrete built-in models.

classes.docSummary: Surface diffusion Laplacian stencil for a scalar field on the disk mesh (radius, normals, stability).

It smooths the ALD Coverage scalar on the disk mesh, not the level-set surface; on every other process it is inert. See docs/ald-surface-diffusion-contract.md and worker/probe_surface_diffusion_native.py.

partialExposurePolicy: advanced-parameter-or-output-not-exposed rows may still carry exposedBy when a strict subset of the class is reachable; those rows set partialExposure=true.
workbenchExposureGaps: docs/capabilities.json lists only isotropic and singleParticle under 'models'; the 14 exposed specialized models are documented in backend/specialized_models.py and /api/specialized-models, not in the capability file.
No single document previously mapped the native class surface (including parameter objects and enums) to the project schema; this matrix is that map.

spxOnly.why: Not a ViennaPS model. The engine only consumes already-patterned masks (GDS or geometry).
spxOnly.workbenchStatus: absent; a GDS mask is the closest substitute

spxOnly.why: No thermal budget or dopant diffusion solver in viennaps 4.6.2.
No silicide reaction/diffusion model. MaterialCategory.Silicide is a label, not a process.
Only Oxidation has an internal mask-mechanics solver; there is no general stress model.
Planarize is a geometric cut; the workbench adds a measured stop material, not a CMP model.

spxOnly.capability: Doping profiles and device/electrical simulation (IV, CV, contacts)
spxOnly.why: ViennaPS is a topography engine; no device or field solver.

spxOnly.capability: Contact/M0 metal routing as a process step
spxOnly.why: Requires a second mask/geometry stage; not an engine limitation but a project-model limitation.
spxOnly.workbenchStatus: partial: gdsBoolean + continuation can approximate it

batches.title: FaradayCageEtching as a structured specialized model (3D)
batches.notes: cageAngle plus the existing ionBeam parameter group (IBEParameters). Mask materials already come from geometry. The 2D path hung in a bounded probe, so the step must reject 2D at validation time.
acceptanceCriteria: Validator rejects dimension=2 with a clear 422 before the worker starts.
3D single-step run against a trench + mask produces the same surface as a direct native reference within 1e-6 um (max point distance).
An independent native Faraday reference (cage source directions, not ordinary normal-incidence IBE) matches within 1e-6 um.
Replay of the recorded run reproduces the artifact hashes exactly.
specialized-models catalog documents the model with engineVersion 4.6.2 and dimension 3.

batches.title: GeometricTrenchDeposition as a structured specialized model (2D)
batches.notes: Closed-form trench fill, 7 scalar arguments, no flux engine. Exact 2D-only: 3D aborts with SIGSEGV.
acceptanceCriteria: Validator rejects dimension=3 for this model.
2D trench run reproduces the analytic profile of a direct native reference within 1e-6 um.
The step reports that no flux engine was used (engine=not-applicable) in the run execution record.
A degenerate parameter set (zero depositionRate or zero width) fails validation instead of hanging.

batches.title: CSV rate tables: RateGrid + CSVFileProcess
batches.notes: Needs a new uploaded asset kind (like GDS assets) with a fixed CSV schema, size cap and sha256 in the project. Must require an explicit interpolation mode because the engine only logs 'Interpolation mode not set.' and continues with an effectively empty grid. setCustomInterpolator stays unavailable.
acceptanceCriteria: CSV upload is size-capped, hashed, schema-validated (x,z,rate columns, finite floats) and stored under the data directory; the project stores assetId + hash, never a filesystem path.
Missing interpolation mode is a 422, not a warning.
A run with a LINEAR grid matches a direct native reference (same CSV) within 1e-6 um.
Request hash changes when the CSV content changes; replay of the old hash fails with a clear error.
No API field can reach setCustomInterpolator.

batches.title: Particle shape distributions (Box/Sphere/CustomSphere)
batches.notes: Implemented as schema-7 geometry step particleShape (BoxDistribution/SphereDistribution, no duration). Masks come from the project geometry's native mask materials via addMaskMaterial, which is the officially supported combination for negative (etch) displacement: 2D/3D probes keep the protected material in place while the exposed surface shrinks, and the official FinFET example uses the same call. Positive (deposition) displacement with any non-empty mask SIGSEGVs in 2D/3D (material mask, raw viennals mask from getMaterialLevelSet, applyToSingleMaterial, insertMask; near, far or full-domain mask), so depositions stay maskless and the run record lists the omitted mask materials. ViennaPS 4.7.0 / ViennaLS 5.10.0 still crash identically and the upstream source still carries the positive-box-with-mask TODO. CustomSphereDistribution aborts in 2D and 3D even without a mask (returnCode -6, 'Point ID 3 is out of bounds for CustomSphereDistribution with 3 radii!'), so it stays unexposed. Evidence: docs/particle-shape-distribution-contract.md.
acceptanceCriteria: Design note proves how the viennals mask is built from an existing project domain without a second geometry source of truth: addMaskMaterial over the project's native mask material level sets, the same rule the flux and CSV steps use.
Box and Sphere produce a geometry whose surface mesh equals a direct native reference (no-mask deposit, masked etch, 2D and 3D).
Radii/half-axes are bounded (count and magnitude) and rejected outside range.
CustomSphereDistribution is only exposed after a passing 2D and 3D probe is archived; otherwise it stays out of the catalog.

batches.title: Full plasma sub-parameter families
batches.notes: Implemented by the optional nativeParameters.advanced object plus the parameter-object overloads. The allowlist is the native-consumed subset: inert SiGe fields, Substrate.B_ie, and the SF6C4F8 passivation family are rejected. Advanced defaults for flat-shared fields equal the flat catalog defaults; model-specific native defaults and per-material maps are recorded in run metadata.
acceptanceCriteria: An optional nativeParameters.advanced object is accepted per plasma model with a strict per-model allowlist; unknown/inert keys are rejected.
Omitting the object leaves the request hash of every existing project unchanged.
Advanced defaults for flat-shared fields equal the flat catalog defaults; native-only defaults are read back and recorded in run metadata.
2D and 3D golden runs for sf6o2, hbro2, sf6c4f8 and a cf4o2 SiGe case match independent native references within 1e-6 um; archived docs evidence is still pending.

batches.title: Multi-RateSet directional model
batches.notes: Implemented as steps[].rateSets[] on model:directional, mutually exclusive with the scalar fields. Each set carries its own direction, directional/isotropic velocities, optional maskMaterials and calculateVisibility; 1–8 sets are accepted and the worker uses the native Sequence[RateSet] overload. The scalar form remains the default and keeps historical hashes.
acceptanceCriteria: A rateSets list (1–8 sets) is accepted alongside, and mutually exclusive with, the scalar fields.
Existing directional projects keep their request hashes and results when rateSets is omitted.
A multi-set run matches a direct native reference within 1e-6 um; opposite sets cancel additively.
Per-set maskMaterials are fully supported (including an explicit empty list), not silently ignored.
2D third-component values are normalized before the native call; unsupported scalar/rateSets mixtures are rejected.

batches.title: SurfaceDiffusionParameters for ALD coverage smoothing
batches.notes: The bounded probe found the real insertion point: the ALP strategy builds the stencil only for SingleParticleALD with coverageDiffusionCoefficient > 0, and diffuses the Coverage scalar (not the level-set geometry). Exposed as the optional steps[].surfaceDiffusion object on specialized:ald. Every other model is rejected as inert even when the object is disabled; a zero coverageDiffusionCoefficient is rejected only when surfaceDiffusion is enabled, because a disabled token is a no-op.
acceptanceCriteria: A bounded probe records which process/model accepts surface diffusion and what it changes on a trench.
If no legal insertion point exists in 4.6.2, the class is documented as not applicable and stays unexposed.
If it is inserted, defaults must be a no-op (existing artifact hashes unchanged).
radius/sigmaNormal/stabilityFactor ranges are bounded in the schema with documented units.

batches.title: Generic DenseCellSet output
batches.notes: Exposed as the opt-in outputSettings.cellSet block. The worker builds a generic native DenseCellSet from the current level sets, records counts/grid/fields, and writes VTU and/or JSON artifacts. Sizing is preflighted and re-bounded from the measured surface before allocation; OxideRegrowth output is unchanged. Below-surface sets and readCellSetData continuation remain unexposed.
acceptanceCriteria: A per-step opt-in (height, cover material, periodic flag, format, scalar labels) is validated before the run.
The existing OxideRegrowth artifact keeps its exact schema and hash.
Artifact size is preflighted (24 B/cell VTU + 64 KiB JSON) and an oversized cell set fails before writing/allocating.
Cell counts and field arrays replay byte-identically for a fixed seed, including lazy materialization.
2D, 3D and periodic native runs produce real VTU/JSON artifacts; omitted block keeps historical hashes.

batches.title: Oxidation advanced setters and Si110
batches.notes: Si110 plus the optional steps[].advancedOxidation object. Four solver setters are exposed only after controlled native probes showed a deterministic surface-hash change: cflFactor, mechanicsTolerance, couplingTolerance and simplePressureRelaxation. GPU mode, maxGridPoints, solve bounds, iteration caps, pressure/stokes tolerance, simpleVelocityRelaxation, mask mechanics and the legacy OxidationParameters names stay out with recorded evidence. Defaults are installed-native defaults and materialising them is a behaviour no-op.
acceptanceCriteria: Si110 exists in the installed enum, changes the planar native readback and produces distinct 2D/3D surface hashes.
Advanced setters are grouped in strict steps[].advancedOxidation; omitted block keeps historical request hashes and artifacts.
Every accepted setter has a controlled native probe showing a deterministic surface-hash change.
Excluded/inert members are rejected by the strict schema, not silently ignored; no raw native object or pointer is accepted.
Mask mechanics and GPU oxidation stay out until a verified host run exists.

batches.title: Deliberately never exposed: generic Python process models and callbacks
batches.notes: These are extension hooks. Accepting them would execute arbitrary Python inside the worker, break request hashing and replay, escape the bounded-child resource model, and make results non-reproducible. MultiParticleProcess already covers the legitimate use case with declarative coefficients.
acceptanceCriteria: No API field, project schema field or replay field can name a Python callable or module path.
A schema-level test asserts these names never appear in project/replay JSON.
Any new modelling need is met by a declarative field plus a native reference run, not a callback.
